correctness.rationale: For either anytime schedule and fixed k≥1, conditional on positive consecutive boundaries (a,A,B,C), the three u_{k-1},u_k,u_{k+1} are independent uniforms on (a,A),(A,B),(B,C) even when boundaries themselves are random. Let x=A-u_{k-1}>=0 and y=u_k-A>=0. Then D=(A-x)^-2-(A+y)^-2=2(x+y)/A^3+O((x+y)^2), while numerator tends to A^-2-u_{k+1}^-2>0; β>t is asymptotically a triangle x+y<(A^3/2t)(A^-2-u_{k+1}^-2). Its area is A^6(A^-2-u_{k+1}^-2)^2/(8t^2). Integrating the third uniform yields exact positive constant A^6/(8(A-a)(B-A)(C-B))∫_B^C(A^-2-v^-2)^2 dv. Dominated convergence gives fixed-boundary asymptotic; for fixed k the random-boundary law has bounded away from zero/above positive interval lengths and A, giving dominated averaging. Survival t^-2 and tail-moment identity Eβ^r=r∫t^{r-1}P(β>t)dt establish finite r<2 and infinite r≥2. The fixed-time terminal schedule is excluded as required.
